sections.html:
Since December 1, 1902 Denver has been both a city and a county. Where other places have a city hall and a separate courthouse, here a single government does both jobs. About 715,522 people lived in its 78 official neighborhoods at the 2020 count, with Adams, Arapahoe and Jefferson counties around the edges.

For a seller that means fewer stops. One city government employs the Assessor who prices your house, the Treasury staff who bill it and the Recorder who files the deed. Hail is the weather problem people bring up, because Denver sits tenth among U.S. cities of 50,000 or more for hailstorm exposure. Expect buyers to ask how old the roof is.

sections.h2: How the Denver tax bill is calculated
sections.html:
Take actual value, subtract a value reduction, multiply by an assessment rate, then multiply by the mill levy. The Assessor's FAQ gives these 2024 inputs:

Property typeValue reduction per parcelAssessment rate
Residential$55,0006.7%
Commercial improved$30,00027.9%
All other$027.9%

Denver's combined general mill levy for 2024 came to 79.202 mills, or 0.079202 as a decimal. Taxing authorities settle on levies every December and neither levies nor rates stay put, so rely on your own bill for current numbers.

Real property gets a fresh appraisal in odd-numbered years only. A house is priced by the market approach, which looks at sales in the two years that ended the previous June 30.

sections.h2: Due dates and the yearly calendar
sections.html:
You have two ways to pay: halves on the last day of February and June 15, or a single payment by April 30. Treasury's calendar covers the rest of the year:

  • January: yearly tax statements go in the mail.
  • April 1: last day to apply for a deferral.
  • April 15: personal property declarations.
  • April 30: full payment, plus the cutoff for the elderly and disabled refund application.
  • May through August: notices go to delinquent accounts.
  • July 1: later delinquencies open up for tax lien buyers to endorse.
  • July 15: senior and disabled veteran exemption applications.
  • September and October: delinquent taxes appear in a newspaper notice.
  • October: the real estate tax lien auction.

For an exact payoff on a delinquent account, including penalty and interest, call Treasury.

Mark June 8 on the calendar every year. If it falls on a weekend or holiday you get the next business day. Your Notice of Valuation explains how to submit in writing, in person or online.

A good protest names your parcel or schedule number, gives a phone number you will answer in the daytime, and states plainly why the value is off. Back it up with sales of comparable houses or evidence of problems like a bad foundation or failing roof. Lose, and you can still take it to the State Board of Assessment Appeals, to District Court, or to binding arbitration.

Skipped a protest in the past? You may reach back up to two earlier years with a petition to the Board of County Commissioners for abatement or refund of taxes.

sections.h2: Deferral for seniors and active military
sections.html:
Through the county treasurer, Colorado allows certain owners to put off paying. The application window is January 1 to April 1, and eligible groups are owners 65 or older and active-duty military.

A senior applicant must reach 65 by December 31, occupy the house, be current on earlier taxes, owe no more than 75 percent of actual value in liens and mortgages, and carry no reverse mortgage. Active-duty applicants meet another test: liens, mortgages and deferrals combined must stay below 100 percent of actual value with a VA-guaranteed loan, or 90 percent without.

What you defer is really a loan, recorded behind your mortgage as a junior lien and accruing interest from May 1. Sign a sale contract and repayment comes due within 90 days. Request the payoff figure early so your title company can fold it into closing.

Storm drain and sanitary sewer service are billed on their own statements, and an unpaid one can cling to the property alongside regular tax. Storm drain bills arrive in February, April, June and August; sewer bills in March, May, July and September.

Title searchers will spot any unpaid service lien and list it as a payoff. Get the balance from Treasury before you put the house up. For other city questions, dial 3-1-1, or (720) 913-1311 from outside Denver.

Taxes that stay unpaid through summer are advertised in September and October, and the real estate tax lien auction follows in October. Buyers at the auction are paying your tax in return for a claim, which then has to be cleared before a clean sale. Delinquency notices start in May, so the sooner you deal with a balance, the fewer steps remain.

If a notice arrives for an account you believe is paid, gather your payment dates and the parcel ID and contact Treasury quickly. A wrong notice left alone can still drift toward the sale list.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
Pull together your latest tax statement, your Notice of Valuation and any deferral paperwork. Note whether you protested this year and whether a protest is still open. If your mortgage includes escrow, ask the lender for its payment history so the title officer can match it against what Treasury shows.

Sellers who inherited a house should also locate any storm drain or sewer statements, since those are separate from the main bill and easy to miss. Ask the title company early which of the three items, tax, service lien or deferral, show a balance, so no payoff surprises you at the closing table. Seniors and disabled owners who claimed an exemption should confirm it is still in place, because the July 15 application date comes around every year and a lapse can raise the next bill.

A tax balance is not a barrier to selling. Treasury gives the title company a figure, and the money is taken from your sale proceeds, so nothing comes out of pocket beforehand. Typical order of events:

  1. The current balance is pulled, along with any earlier years still open.
  2. The title search surfaces service liens, a deferral lien and anything sold at the October auction.
  3. Each one turns into a payoff line on the settlement statement.
  4. Treasury is paid when the sale closes.

Once a lien has been sold, the buyer's payoff is owed on top of the tax, which is where an experienced Denver title officer earns their fee. If you think a delinquent notice is wrong, write to propertytaxinfo@denvergov.org with your parcel ID, address and payment dates.

Behind on tax, or inherited a Denver house you don't want? We can send a written cash offer for it in its current condition. A cash sale skips the repairs and showings, and the decision stays with you.

faqs.q: When is Denver property tax due?
faqs.a: Either split it between the last day of February and June 15, or pay it all by April 30. A weekend or holiday pushes the date to the next business day.

faqs.q: What is the Denver property tax protest deadline?
faqs.a: June 8, or the next business day if that is a weekend or holiday. Your Notice of Valuation explains how to file.

faqs.q: What was Denver's mill levy in 2024?
faqs.a: Denver's combined general levy came to 79.202 mills. Because levies change each December, check your current bill.

faqs.q: How often does Denver reappraise homes?
faqs.a: In odd-numbered years only. Values reflect sales from the two years ending the previous June 30.

faqs.q: Does selling a Denver house trigger the property tax deferral repayment?
faqs.a: Yes. Under the state program, a sale or contract of sale starts a 90 day clock for repayment.
